verdict.rationale: Mastra's own docs describe recurring autonomous execution: workflows can declare a cron `schedule` that Mastra fires, agents can run on a cron cadence, and background tasks let long-running tool calls proceed without blocking the agent loop. Durable goals keep an agent working toward an objective across iterations, and the engine documents pausing and resuming via persisted state. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of scheduler operation (hosting requirements, failure and retry handling for scheduled runs), independent or hands-on corroboration that scheduled or background automations run reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Declare a `schedule` field on a workflow and Mastra will fire it on the cron you specify.
A schedule runs an agent on a cron cadence.
Background tasks let an agent dispatch a long-running tool call without blocking the agentic loop.
A goal is a durable, thread-scoped objective: a standing instruction the agent keeps working toward across loop iterations until a judge model decides it's satisfied
Mastra uses storage to remember execution state, so you can pause indefinitely and resume where you left off.
